title: Lemon Curd
subtitle: Sharp, smooth lemon curd for spreading or filling
excerpt: Egg yolks, butter, sugar, and lots of fresh lemon juice, gently cooked over low heat until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. A vivid yellow, intensely lemony curd.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lemon curd was developed in Britain in the 19th century as a preserve for spreading on scones and bread. Early recipes used only egg yolks and butter: the whites were considered wasteful. Modern versions typically use whole eggs. The curd is cooked over a gentle heat or in a bain-marie: too high a temperature and the eggs scramble. It keeps for up to two weeks in a sterilised jar in the fridge and is used as a spread, a cake filling, a tart filling, or a swirl through Greek yoghurt.

content.text: Keep the heat low throughout: patience is the technique here. Stir constantly so the eggs do not scramble at the edges. The curd is done when it coats the back of a spoon and a line drawn through it with your finger stays clean. It thickens further as it cools, so remove from the heat while it still feels a little thin.
Whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, caster sugar, lemon juice, and lemon zest in a heavy-based saucepan.

Add the butter cubes. Set over very low heat. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula, for 10 to 15 minutes until the curd has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil.
Pour through a fine sieve into sterilised jars to remove the zest. Seal and leave to cool. Refrigerate once cool. Use within 2 weeks.
